text.p: Albania's government ordered the re-start of the national soccer championship on Monday.
The league had been suspended for one month because of unrest sparked by the collapse of five pyramid investment schemes.
State sports secretary Marjeta Zace told the country's soccer federation to resume matches this weekend, changing the venue of any potential trouble spots.
A friendly against Macedonia was cancelled last week and the federation was hoping that World Cup qualifers with Ukraine and Germany on March 29 and April 2 respectively would remain unaffected.
Albania was suspended briefly by FIFA last year after the sports ministry removed the chairman of the country's soccer federation, Eduard Dervishi, and dissolved the executive committee.
Argentine World Cup player Mario Kempes, who has a two-year contract to coach first division Lushnje, has left the club until the situation calms down.
Lushnje were sponsored by Pellumb Xhaferri, detained chief of one of the collapsed pyramid investment schemes.
Officials also said Brazilians Edu and Valdemir Souza dos Santos snapped up by Lushnje -- Albania's first club to buy foreign players -- had left the country because of the problems.
